title: Spectrally Selective Charging of an Interacting Quantum Battery via an Anharmonic Mediator
authors: Sujay Mondal, Anumita Mukhopadhyay, Siddhartha Dutta, Abhijit Bandyopadhyay
abstract: We investigate a finite-time quantum-battery charging architecture in which a driven two-level working system transfers nonequilibrium resources to an interacting two-qubit battery through a weakly anharmonic three-level mediator. Finite-time driving generates coherence and ergotropy, while excitation-number conservation organizes the transfer into distinct dynamical sectors. The mediator then provides spectrally selective charging channels: its lower transition enables nearly complete single-excitation transfer with negligible residual mediator energy, whereas initial mediator loading activates a cross-resonant two-excitation cascade toward the doubly excited battery state. The latter exhibits a modest reduction in transfer efficiency due to the unequal collective matrix elements of the effective three-state chain. Detuning scans quantify the spectral tolerance, and the full mixed-state dynamics reveals distinct energy- and ergotropy-transfer profiles. Finite-time compression, thermal reset, and switching work close the cycle-level energy balance to numerical precision. The resulting scheme combines nonequilibrium resource generation, spectral selectivity, coherent multilevel charging, and thermodynamic cycle closure within a single architecture.
summary: This work proposes a novel quantum battery charging cycle using a three-level mediator to mediate energy transfer from a driven working system to an interacting two-qubit battery. The authors show that by controlling the driving time, they can generate non-equilibrium resources like ergotropy, which facilitates spectrally selective, coherent charging pathways. The entire process is rigorously closed by accounting for work and heat during the cycle reset.
main_problem: The paper investigates a quantum-battery charging architecture that combines nonequilibrium resource generation with spectrally selective energy transfer.
main_result: The scheme successfully demonstrates a complete cycle, achieving near-perfect energy balance while enabling controlled, selective charging of the battery using a mediator.
method: The analysis uses time-dependent quantum dynamics simulations to track energy, coherence, and ergotropy transfer across multiple coupled subsystems.
model_or_system: The system consists of a driven two-level working system (S), an interacting two-qubit battery (B), and a weakly anharmonic three-level mediator (M). The dynamics are governed by a total Hamiltonian incorporating time-dependent couplings.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mediator providing distinct transition frequencies for spectral selectivity, and the cycle closure is confirmed by tracking work and heat terms.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Mediator-assisted charging cycle. (i) The working system S is thermalized at fixed control ξh. (ii) An isolated finite-time expansion drives ξh →ξc over a duration τe. (iii) At fixed ξc, the nonequilibrium resource generated in S is coherently transferred to the interacting two-qubit battery B through the three-level mediator M. (iv) The working system is isolated and compressed back to ξh, after which rethermalization restores its initial Gibbs state.

Figure 2: Finite-time resource generation during expansion. (a) Nonadiabatic transition probability Pe, (b) coherence C(e) S in the final energy basis, (c) working-system energy change ∆Ee = E(e) S −E(h) S , and (d) ergotropy We versus expansion duration τe. The initial Gibbs state has β = 5 and ξh = 4, and the different curves correspond to the indicated values of (∆S, ξc).

Fig. 2 shows the resource generated by a linear protocol, f(t/τe) = t/τe, over 0.10 ≤τe ≤10.0. Since | ˙ξ| = |ξc −ξh|/τe, short expansion times correspond to strong nonadiabatic driving, while increasing τe drives the dynamics toward the adiabatic limit [18–20]. Accordingly, short strokes produce finite Pe, coherence, and ergotropy, whereas all three are suppressed as the dynamics approaches adiabatic following. The total energy change instead approaches the finite adiabatic contribution associated with the reduction of the instantaneous gap. The expansion thus converts the initial thermal population imbalance into a controllable nonequi- librium resource for the subsequent charging stroke.

Figure 3: Energy-level structure during the transfer stroke. The couplings J(t) and g(t) mediate sequential S–M and M–B excitation exchange. The interacting battery is charged through the symmetric ladder |00B⟩↔|B+⟩↔|11B⟩, while |B−⟩remains dark.
